title: World Cricketers' Association Slams ICC Over Changes to 2027 ODI World Cup Format
excerpt: <pThe World Cricketers' Association (WCA) has publicly criticized the International Cricket Council's decision to revise the format of the 2027 Men's ODI World Cup, calling the sudden changes a threat to transparency,…
body:
The World Cricketers' Association (WCA) has publicly criticized the International Cricket Council's decision to revise the format of the 2027 Men's ODI World Cup, calling the sudden changes a threat to transparency, global growth, and the careers of players from emerging nations.

What Changed

The ICC has retained the 14-team structure for the tournament, which will be hosted across South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia. However, it has introduced a new three-stage format: a preliminary Super Series for the three lowest-ranked qualifying teams, followed by a group stage, a Super 7 round, and then the knockout phase. This replaces the originally planned two-groups-of-seven format.

WCA's Objections

"The ICC is entitled to determine the structure of its global events. However, when commitments are made to the game, qualification pathways are established and countries and players invest years pursuing those opportunities, significant changes deserve genuine consultation, transparency and a clear explanation," WCA CEO Tom Moffat said during the association's Annual Conference in Edinburgh.

The WCA outlined objections across four pillars: transparency, meaningful consultation, global growth, and impact on players. Moffat emphasized that players from smaller nations may have dedicated their entire careers to qualifying for a World Cup, only to find the goalposts moved mid-cycle.

Concerns About Cricket's Global Expansion

The WCA argued that the revised format "fundamentally dilutes the opportunity originally promised to emerging nations." Under the new Super Series preliminary round, the lowest-ranked qualifiers are effectively relegated to a play-in tournament, limiting their guaranteed exposure against established Test-playing nations.

"It is difficult to reconcile the game's stated ambition of growing cricket globally with decisions that reduce meaningful opportunities at pinnacle events for some of the countries that stood to benefit most from genuine expansion," Moffat added.

The Broader Significance

Moffat framed the issue as going beyond one tournament. "This isn't simply about the format of one tournament. It's about ensuring game-wide confidence in how the game makes major strategic decisions," he said, referencing the WCA's Global Game Structure Report calling for greater transparency in cricket governance.

The 2027 ODI World Cup is particularly significant for India, which will be looking to defend the sport's premier 50-over title. For the Indian diaspora worldwide, the format decisions will shape how accessible and competitive the tournament experience will be.
nri_angle: Cricket is central to the Indian diaspora; format changes directly affect how India and emerging nations compete
